scope: Scoped re-check after the move from Combined Science: exam-structure claims, required-practical numbers, tier wrappers, course-scope labels and board naming. Facts, numbers and answer keys were checked earlier today on the source unit and were not re-checked.

findings.claim: In Combined Science, calculation questions on energy are very common.
findings.truth: This lesson now sits on GCSE Physics: two papers, each 1 hour 45 minutes, 100 marks, 50% of the GCSE, Foundation and Higher tiers. Reworded to 'In GCSE Physics'.

findings.claim: There are three main types you need to know for combined science: alpha, beta and gamma.
findings.truth: Combined Science reference removed. The spec list itself (alpha, beta, gamma, neutron) is identical on both courses, so only the course name was wrong.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.2.1 Radioactive decay and nuclear radiation

findings.claim: The whole of content_html sits inside one div with class higher-only, which on the Combined unit meant 'separate science only'.
findings.truth: On the Physics course gas pressure and the particle model (4.3.3.1), Boyle's law (4.3.3.2 Pressure in gases, physics only) and atmospheric pressure (4.5.5.2) carry no HT flag, so they are core. Only 4.5.5.1.2 Pressure in a fluid 2 is (HT only), covering p = h x rho x g and upthrust and floating. The whole-lesson wrapper is removed and two wrappers are written in its place: one around Pressure in Fluids, one around Upthrust and Floating. Tags stay balanced: two openings, two closings.
findings.evidence: spec 4.3.3.1, 4.3.3.2, 4.3.3.3 (HT only, work done on a gas, not taught here), 4.5.5.1.2 (HT only), 4.5.5.2

findings.truth: The prefix was the deck-level 'separate science only' marker. Eight cards are core content on the Physics course, so the prefix is removed from those. Seven cards (column of liquid, depth, density, upthrust, floating, sinking, the steel ship) sit in 4.5.5.1.2 and keep it.

findings.claim: 'Star Formation and the Life Cycle of Stars' is taught in a Paper 1 unit with no paper label, ending 'the key point for GCSE is that fusion is the energy source that powers all stars'.
findings.truth: The life cycle of a star is spec 4.8.1.2, inside topic 8 Space physics, which Paper 2 assesses. A short 'covered in Paper 2' pointer is added. No label said 'beyond the combined course', so none had to be removed.
findings.evidence: spec 4.8.1.2 The life cycle of a star; spec 2.2 Paper 2 covers topics 5 to 8

findings.claim: The 'Calculating Total Resistance in Parallel' box teaches 1/Rtotal = 1/R1 + 1/R2, the exam tip tells students to find 1/Rtotal first, and the 6-mark question asks for the total resistance of three lamps in parallel.
findings.truth: The Physics spec carries the same exclusion as Combined: students are not required to calculate the total resistance of two resistors joined in parallel. The physics and the arithmetic are right (6 and 12 give 4 ohms; three 6-ohm lamps give 2 ohms), so nothing is wrong, only out of scope. No 'beyond the combined course' label is present, so nothing had to be removed. Options: cut the box, the tip line and the calculation half of the 6-mark question, or keep it as stretch. Carried forward unchanged, matching today's ruling on the Combined unit.

findings.claim: The second half of the lesson teaches pressure in a fluid, atmospheric pressure and upthrust inside a unit called Physics Paper 1.
findings.truth: Spec 4.5.5 Pressure and pressure differences in fluids sits in topic 5 Forces, which Paper 2 assesses. Gas pressure and Boyle's law (4.3.3) are correctly on Paper 1. Options: move the three fluid sections into the Physics Paper 2 unit, or add a 'covered in Paper 2' line as in lesson 11. Not edited, because either choice moves a large block and needs your call.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.5, 4.5.5.2; spec 2.2 Paper 1 covers topics 1 to 4

findings.truth: No lesson in this unit states a practical number. Lesson 3 says 'One of your required practicals', lesson 6 heads a section 'Measuring Density - Required Practical' and lesson 7 'The SHC Required Practical'. All three describe the right method for the Physics list (I-V is practical 4, specific heat capacity 1, density 5), so nothing needed renumbering. Required practical 2 (physics only), thermal insulators, is not named anywhere; lesson 2 mentions thermal insulation only as a way to reduce unwanted energy transfers.
findings.evidence: spec 8.2.1 to 8.2.10 (the ten physics required practicals)

findings.claim: The exam tip and the second and third key takeaways both use p = h x rho x g and upthrust.
findings.truth: Both are Higher-tier content (4.5.5.1.2) and neither field can carry a tier wrapper in this template, so a Foundation student still meets them. No edit available; worth knowing if tier flags are ever added to those fields.

summary: 11 lessons re-checked against GCSE Physics 8463 after the move. Two Combined Science references removed (lessons 1 and 8); no lesson ever stated a paper count, duration or mark total, and no lesson names the board. Lesson 10's whole-lesson Higher wrapper is replaced by two wrappers covering only 4.5.5.1.2, and eight of its fifteen flashcards lose the '(Higher)' prefix. Lesson 11 gains a 'covered in Paper 2' pointer on the star life cycle. No sentence anywhere told a student a topic was 'not on your course', 'separate science only' or 'beyond the combined course'. Two paper-allocation questions are left for adjudication.
